sheet-1-1.description: The northern half of the borough of Wenonah, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north lies to the right. The part runs from Mantua Avenue along the left edge to Buttonwood Street on the right, and from Lincoln Avenue at the top to Marion Avenue near the bottom, with one further block (number 45) between Marion Avenue and Princeton Street in the lower left corner. Poplar and Elm cross the grid between Mantua Avenue and Buttonwood. The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) crosses the middle of the sheet between West West Jersey Avenue and East West Jersey Avenue, with the passenger station and its platforms at the Mantua Avenue end. The blocks are almost entirely residential: detached frame dwellings, many with stables and sheds, set on large lots, with whole blocks east of Buttonwood (30, 40, 41) only partly built and lots on the north edge of town still empty. Named buildings are the Episcopal Church on Monroe Avenue near Poplar, the Y.M.C.A. in the block between Mantua Avenue, Poplar, Clinton Avenue and Marion Avenue, and the Wenonah Public Schools (a brick school and a stone building) between Elm and Buttonwood south of East West Jersey Avenue, with the town stand pipe, 100 feet high, beside them. A diagonal 66 foot road leaves the corner of Jefferson Avenue and Buttonwood towards the pumping station, about 800 feet away. Water pipes with their sizes, hydrants and house numbers are marked along every street. The sheet number of the adjoining sheet 2 appears at both sides of the railroad.
notes: Lincoln, Jefferson, Monroe, Clinton and Marion Avenue are North Lincoln, North Jefferson, North Monroe, North Clinton and North Marion Avenue today; Princeton Street is North Princeton Avenue.
West West Jersey Avenue and East West Jersey Avenue, either side of the railroad, are North West Avenue and North East Avenue today.
Poplar, Elm and Buttonwood are West and East Poplar, Elm and Buttonwood Street today (West of the railroad, East of it).
Mantua Avenue is drawn 100 feet wide; West Mantua Avenue and East Mantua Avenue today.
The West Jersey & Seashore R.R. (P.R.R.) is the Vineland Secondary line in OpenStreetMap.
The diagonal road to the pumping station east of Buttonwood is not in the modern street data.

Scale 100 ft to an inch, turned on the page (north to the right). North half of Wenonah: Mantua Av to Buttonwood St, Lincoln Av to Marion Av, with the West Jersey & Seashore R.R. between W. and E. West Jersey Av (today North West and North East Avenue). Title cartouche, key and water/fire text notched out of the mask. Part 2 (inset, 50 ft to an inch): Wenonah Pumping Station by a lake and an unnamed road, about 800 ft from Buttonwood St and Jefferson Av; not configured.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Wenonah Pumping Station (50 ft to an inch), a road and a lake (no street junction; only a road with no name and a lake shore; needs identify the 1922 pumping station site and the road on modern data, then step 6b).

sheet-2-1.description: The southern half of the borough of Wenonah, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north lies to the right. The part runs from Pine Street along the left edge to Mantua Avenue on the right, and from Lincoln Avenue at the top to Princeton Avenue at the bottom; Cedar, Willow and Cherry cross the grid between them. The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) crosses the sheet between West West Jersey Avenue and East West Jersey Avenue, with a freight house at the Mantua Avenue end. At the top a curved street runs north from Willow past large blocks (2, 8, 9) that are mostly vacant, with poultry houses on several lots. The business centre lies on Sioux Place, a short private street between Cherry and Mantua Avenue, with a bakery, a store, a fire department house and the public library nearby. South of the railroad are Wenonah Park, the Wenonah Military Academy with its drill hall, chemical laboratory and power plant between Cherry and Mantua Avenue, its athletic field on Pine Street, the Wenonah Carnation Gardens greenhouses, the Wenonah M.E. Church on Clinton Avenue and the Memorial Presbyterian Church at Mantua Avenue and Princeton Avenue. The rest is detached frame housing on large lots. The lower left corner is taken by a framed inset of block 25, which is configured as a separate part. Water pipes, hydrants and house numbers are marked along the streets.
notes: The street between Clinton Avenue and Princeton Avenue is lettered Mantua Avenue on this sheet, while sheet 1 letters the same street Marion Avenue; it is South Marion Avenue today. Mantua Avenue proper is the 100 foot street on the right edge.
Lincoln, Jefferson, Monroe, Clinton and Princeton Avenue are South Lincoln, South Jefferson, South Monroe, South Clinton and South Princeton Avenue today.
West West Jersey Avenue and East West Jersey Avenue are South West Avenue and South East Avenue today.
Cedar, Willow and Cherry are West and East Cedar, Willow and Cherry Street today; Pine is East Pine Street.
Sioux Place is marked Arbitrary (a private street with arbitrary house numbers); it is not in the modern street data.
The junction of Willow with West West Jersey Avenue was left out of the fit: the detector placed it on lettering about 10 ft off.

Scale 100 ft to an inch, turned on the page (north to the right). South half of Wenonah: Pine St to Mantua Av, Lincoln Av to Princeton Av; Wenonah Military Academy, Wenonah Park, carnation greenhouses. The street between Clinton Av and Princeton Av is printed MANTUA AV. here (MARION AV. on sheet 1; today South Marion Avenue). Part 2: inset in a heavy frame at the lower left, block 25 at Princeton Av and Mantua Av, same scale and rotation; placed from one hand-picked junction.

sheet-2-2.description: A framed inset in the lower left corner of sheet 2, drawn at the main sheet's scale of 100 feet to an inch and with the same orientation (north to the right), showing block 25 at the corner of Princeton Avenue and Mantua Avenue, which lies just beyond the edge of the main map. The frame follows Princeton Avenue along the top and Mantua Avenue down the right side, then runs diagonally to the lower left, so only the block's two street fronts are drawn and the streets themselves are cut by the frame. The block holds a large stone and frame dwelling of two and a half stories with a basement, set back 195 feet from Mantua Avenue, a tool house, a two storey dwelling with an auto house near Mantua Avenue, and a group of dwellings and outbuildings numbered 133 1/2 near the lower left. Water pipes of three inches are marked in both streets, and a large figure 2 with its own north arrow marks the inset.
notes: Princeton Avenue is South Princeton Avenue today; Mantua Avenue is East Mantua Avenue.

Placed from one hand-picked point at the junction centre (block corner plus half the street widths, 100 ft for Mantua Avenue and 66 ft for Princeton Avenue) with the main sheet's scale and rotation; the junction centre lies outside the frame. Low confidence: perhaps 5 to 10 m.
